L2.source: sealed experiment d4908236 (pooled over 5 runs of hash a99ceef28136)

finding: L1 measures -0.295 deg (n=6, one run) against L2 -0.449 (n=30) and L5 -0.832 (n=25) on the same reviewed protocol family and rig. L1 is the smallest of the three legs measured so far, widening the observed per-leg spread to about 2.8x between L1 and L5. L1 and L5 per-cycle ranges do NOT overlap. L1 and L2 per-cycle ranges DO overlap ([-0.448,-0.176] vs [-0.615,-0.263]), so L1-vs-L2 separation rests on the means, not on disjoint distributions, and L1 is a single run against L2's five. This strengthens the case that a single global backlash constant mis-compensates the legs, and supports a per-leg table, but L1 needs replicate runs before its value is as firm as L2's or L5's.
caveats: L1 loop widths are only 2-5 encoder counts (resolution 0.0879 deg/count); the per-cycle values are coarsely quantized and L1 sits closest to that floor of the three legs.
L1 sd 0.123 deg is larger than L2 (0.081) and L5 (0.065), consistent with the smaller signal against a fixed quantization step.
Repeat 1 was the largest loop in both L1 attempts (-0.448 here, -0.668 in the aborted attempt 1), suggesting a first-cycle settling effect; excluding it would lower the L1 mean further.
The mid-run return to logical zero did not clear the offset (block A -0.267, block B -0.323), matching the L2 and L5 behaviour.
